svg.title: Three aggregates over orders: every row steps each state; the finish makes one row
svg.text: SELECT count(*), count(customer_id), sum(total) FROM orders;
orders, as the Scan hands them up

g.title: Order 10 (customer_id 1, total 30): both counts add one, to 1 and 1; sum(total) adds 30: 0 + 30 = 30.
Order 11 (customer_id 3, total 15): both counts add one, to 2 and 2; sum(total) adds 15: 30 + 15 = 45.
Order 12 (customer_id 1, total 50): both counts add one, to 3 and 3; sum(total) adds 50: 45 + 50 = 95.
Order 13 (customer_id 2, total 20): both counts add one, to 4 and 4; sum(total) adds 20: 95 + 20 = 115.
Order 14 (customer_id 3, total 5): both counts add one, to 5 and 5; sum(total) adds 5: 115 + 5 = 120.
Order 15: count(*) counts the row (6); its customer_id is NULL, so count(customer_id) skips it and stays at 5; sum(total) adds 40: 160.
The input is done. The finish turns each state into its answer, and one row comes out: 6|5|160. Order 15 is in count(*) and sum(total), not in count(customer_id).
